data.title: Positioning review: "shared context of the work in the repository"
body: # Positioning review: "shared context of the work in the repository"
- **Occasion:** a proposal to shift the product from sprint analytics to shared context of the work for the developer, the PM and the AI agent
- **Method:** market scan (Tavily, September 2026) + assumption map (Torres, 8 categories) + cross-check against the [positioning](DOC-29) and the [competitive snapshot](DOC-41)
- **Conclusion:** **change — yes, but not to what was proposed.** Details below
## 1. What exactly was proposed

> kadence is a work management tool that lives in the repository. The whole team — developer, PM, agent — has a single context: tasks, decisions, documentation next to the code. The agent works without MCP and without external services. The PM can write a technical specification relying on the code already written. Private interaction with no extra tools.
Below I check this thesis part by part rather than as a whole: three of its parts are true, two are dangerous.
## 2. What the market showed
This is not abstract reasoning — as of September 2026 the niche is filled, and filled by strong players.
| Player | What it does | Why it matters to us |

| **[GitHub Spec Kit](https://github.github.com/spec-kit)** | GitHub's official tool. MIT, the `specify` CLI, a `.specify/` directory in the repository, the cycle Spec → Plan → Tasks → Implement, each phase producing a markdown artifact. **38 integrations with agents** | This is **literally the concept we are discussing**, and it is already the standard. In 2026 "every major tool has its own variety of SDD" |

| **[Beads](https://betterstack.com/community/guides/ai/beads-issue-tracker-ai-agents)** (Steve Yegge) | a git-native issue tracker **specifically for AI agents**: SQLite + git, dependencies, the `bd ready` queue, memory between sessions | Directly solves "context amnesia" — the thing we would like to name as our problem |

| **Backlog.md** | Markdown tasks in git, a TUI, a web UI, MCP, three review checkpoints | 6.6k stars. And in their rhetoric: "MCP is the preferred native way, we **also support CLI commands for legacy AI agents**" |
| **OpenSpec, Kiro (AWS), Tessl, BMAD** | One more layer of SDD tools | The category is not empty but overcrowded |
| **Vibe Kanban** | Agent orchestration, parallel worktrees | Lays claim to the same screen |
Two facts that hit the wording of the proposal directly:

1. **"Without MCP" has stopped being an advantage.** A 2026 review of PM tools says it plainly: "Providing an MCP server for your product is becoming a competitive requirement". And Backlog.md already calls CLI agents *legacy*. Our phrase "no MCP, no token, no network" in 2026 reads not as "simple" but as "behind the times".

2. **PMs really do come into the terminal — but through an agent.** "PMs are adopting Claude Code, the engineer's CLI, to write specs, generate tickets, and run product workflows". That is, the assumption about the PM in the repository is **not wrong**, but it works in only one scenario: the PM talks to an agent, and the agent reads and writes the files. A PM with a git client and `kadence ui` is a fantasy.
## 3. Three questions the new concept has no answer to
**Question one, the hardest: the agent already has all the context.**

The repository is files, and the agent reads them. `git log` already contains the history. If we say "we give the agent context", the obvious answer from the market is: "it already has it, that is git". A product that sells access to what is accessible anyway has no reason to exist.
**Question two: in what way are we better than GitHub's Spec Kit?**

Not "how do we differ" — in what way **better**. They have 38 integrations, the GitHub brand and a year of adoption. We have zero users. Walking onto their field with the same message is not competition, it is invisibility.
**Question three: what do we lose?**

Sprints, velocity and estimate-vs-actual are **the only thing none of those listed has**. Neither Spec Kit, nor Beads, nor Backlog.md counts what the work cost. Giving that up for the sake of "context" means surrendering the one unoccupied cell and joining the queue for an occupied one.
## 4. Assumption map
Risk Score = Impact × (1 − Confidence). Confidence: high 0.8, medium 0.5, low 0.2.
| # | Assumption | Category | Impact | Confidence | Risk | What to do with it |

| A1 | The agent lacks context, and we give it | value | 10 | low (0.2) | **8.0** | Refuted by the very first question. It has the context — what it lacks is **structure and the history of decisions** |
| A2 | "Without MCP" is an advantage | gtm | 8 | low (0.2) | **6.4** | The market says the opposite. MCP is becoming a requirement, not a surplus |
| A3 | We can compete with Spec Kit on its own field | strategy | 10 | low (0.2) | **8.0** | We cannot. GitHub, 38 integrations, MIT, a year's head start |
| A4 | The PM works inside the repository | usability | 9 | medium (0.5) | **4.5** | Partly true: only through an agent. There will be no direct work by a PM with the CLI/TUI |
| A5 | "A specification from the code" is a value of its own | value | 8 | low (0.2) | **6.4** | Claude Code does this today without any tool at all |
| A6 | The event journal gives what static specs do not | value | 9 | medium (0.5) | **4.5** | **The most interesting assumption.** Spec drift is an acknowledged problem of the category |
| A7 | Teams need velocity | value | 9 | low (0.2) | **7.2** | The old bet, also untested. Probe B has still not been run |
The highest risk is A1 and A3: both belong to the **new** concept, and both are almost certainly wrong.
## 5. What is right in the proposal — and that is no small thing
Three parts hold up:

1. **The work has to live next to the code.** That is already our thesis, and the market confirmed it: Spec Kit, Beads and Backlog.md made the same bet. We were not wrong about the direction — we are simply not alone in it.

2. **The history of decisions is more valuable than a list of tasks.** Here the proposal hits exactly. The code has *what* was done, git has *when*. **Why** is nowhere, and that is precisely what is lost between an agent's sessions.

3. **Drift is a genuine, acknowledged ailment.** A review of SDD tools names it directly: "Static specs do not update during implementation, creating drift on longer tasks". And in the Spec Kit discussions: "Treating temporary session specs as the permanent source of truth simply doesn't scale over time".
The last one is a gift. **Drift is a problem of mutable state. Our append-only journal does not drift by construction.** Not because we are clever, but because we physically cannot rewrite an event.
## 6. Three options
### A. Change nothing
We keep "sprint analytics". Plus: the one unoccupied cell. Minus: the bet is untested, and analytics on its own for a team of three people sounds small.
### B. Change as proposed

"Shared context for the team and the agent, without MCP". Plus: a hot trend. Minus: head-on against Spec Kit and Beads, with the two riskiest assumptions at the base and without a single feature the competitors do not have. **I do not recommend it.**
### C. Synthesis — the journal as the source of truth
Not "context instead of analytics", but **one source from which both follow**.

> Tasks, decisions and time live in the repository as an **immutable event journal**. From it the agent takes the history that is not in the code; the team takes the state that outlives any session; and the manager takes the number for what it cost. None of this is filled in by hand by anyone — it is already recorded.
Why this works where B fails:
| | Spec Kit | Beads | Backlog.md | kadence (C) |
| Work in the repo | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| State for the agent | static specs | SQLite + git | markdown files | **event journal** |
| Drift | **present, acknowledged** | state is mutable | state is mutable | **impossible by construction** |
| History of "why" | no | partly | no | **yes, it is the journal itself** |
| What it cost | no | no | no | **yes** |
| Conflicts on merge | present | binary SQLite | present | **none, measured** |
We do not compete with Spec Kit — we become the thing it lies **beneath**. Spec Kit writes the spec; kadence remembers what happened to it afterwards.
## 7. Recommendation
**We accept C.** The main message shifts from "we count velocity" to "a journal of the work that shows both the past and the price". Velocity stays — but as a consequence, not as the headline.
What specifically changes in the words:
| Was | Becomes |
| Know what a story point actually costs your team | **Your repo remembers what the code cannot: what was decided, by whom, and what it cost** |
| Sprint analytics | A journal of the team's work in the repository |
| "No MCP, no token, no network" as a slogan | "Files first — MCP optional". Drop the bravado, keep the fact |
| The agent reads tasks | The agent reads the **history**: what was tried, what was rejected and why |
| The PM in the role of TUI user | The PM in the role of the one talking to the agent, while the agent reads the journal |
**What I do NOT recommend changing:** append-only, files, offline, `--json`. That is the foundation, and it is exactly what gives the advantage in C.
**What will have to be added to the product** so that the message is not a lie — three things that do not exist now:
1. `kadence decision` — record a decision with its reason. There are comments now, but no "why" event type.
2. `kadence context <task>` — output of everything that happened to a task, in a format fit for pasting into an agent's context.
3. An MCP server **as an optional package** (`kadence-mcp`) that leaves the core without dependencies. Not building it means deliberately staying "legacy" in someone else's rhetoric.
The third item contradicts [CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md) ("no network") only in appearance: MCP is stdio, not the network, and it can live as a separate package without touching the core.
## 8. What will have to be rewritten if we accept C
| Where | Extent |
| `README.md` | the headline, the first three sections, "Honest status" |
| `docs/product/positioning.md` | the value proposition and the differentiation entirely |
| `docs/PRD.md`, `SPEC.md` | the sections on the goal and the boundaries |
| `docs/product/landing-copy.md` | H1, the subheading, sections 3, 4, 8 |
| `docs/design/brand-and-visual-direction.md` | section 2 stays (cadence = closing the cycle works here too) |
| `kadence-site` | `content/copy.ts` almost in full; the section structure is 80% the same |
| `AGENTS.md`, `.kadence/README.md` | the contract for the agent — add `context` and `decision` |
| The product | the three new commands from section 7 |
The right order is this: **words first, then code**. If `kadence context` does not exist, a landing page about history for the agent will be a promise, not a description.
## 9. How to check this cheaply before rewriting everything
1. **One day for a prototype of `kadence context KAD-1`.** If its output does not improve the agent's work noticeably, the thesis about history is wrong, and we stay on A.

> **Postscript 2026-09-07.** The prototype was not needed: [Probe C](DOC-57) measured that `task show --json` already returns that same full history of a task in 948 bytes, and the size does not depend on how many tasks the project has. The separate command was removed. The check in item 1 remains valid — it now costs zero days, because the tool already exists. That it still has not been run is stated plainly in [discovery-2026-09](DOC-23).

2. **Finally run Probe B** — now with two questions instead of one: whether they measure velocity **and** whether they lose context between an agent's sessions. The second question is the more pressing one now.
3. **Compare on ourselves.** This repository already has `.kadence/events/`. Give the agent the journal and see whether it answers "why is this done this way" better than with the code alone.
That is two or three days of work against a complete rewrite of all the materials. The order should be that one.
